answer:
Model gravity-driven sloshing in a rectangular tank using OpenFOAM interFoam solver.
Tank geometry is a rectangular box with dimensions x=1.0 m (length), y=0.6 m (height, gravity direction), z=0.1 m (width).
Gravity vector is g = (0, -9.81, 0).
Tank is half-filled with water; average water depth is 0.3 m.
Mesh is generated with blockMesh, 200 cells in x, 120 cells in y, 20 cells in z, giving a full 3D structured grid.
Initial alpha.water field is set to 0 (air) everywhere by default in the 0/ directory.
The initial free surface is tilted via a staircase approximation in setFields, dividing x into 10 equal slices of width 0.1 m each.
Slice i (i=0 to 9) covers x in [0.1*i, 0.1*(i+1)], y in [0, hi], z in [-1, 1], with alpha.water=1.
Water depth hi follows hi = 0.255 + 0.01*i, yielding hi=0.255 at x=0 and hi=0.345 at x=1.0, with linear increase of 0.01 m per slice.
Initial velocity field is U = (0, 0, 0) everywhere. Initial p_rgh = 0 everywhere.
The disturbance is driven solely by the tilted free surface under gravity with zero initial velocity.
Boundary conditions for left wall (x=0), right wall (x=1.0), front wall (z=-0.05), rear wall (z=0.05), and bottom (y=0) are no-slip: U = noSlip, p_rgh = fixedFluxPressure, alpha.water = zeroGradient.
Boundary condition for the open top face (y=0.6): U = pressureInletOutletVelocity, p_rgh = totalPressure with p0=0, alpha.water = inletOutlet with inletValue=0.
For 2D simplification (z=1 cell only), front and back faces use empty boundary condition; this is NOT used in the present 3D case.
Time integration uses adaptive time stepping with adjustTimeStep yes, initial deltaT 1e-3 s, maxCo 0.5.
Total simulation endTime is 10 seconds.
Output writeInterval is 0.05 seconds of physical time.
Use standard interFoam fvSchemes: Gauss limitedLinear or upwind for divergence of U and alpha fields, Gauss linear for gradient and Laplacian operators.
Use standard interFoam fvSolution: PIMPLE algorithm with appropriate correctors, MULES with nAlphaSubCycles=1, cAlpha=1, nAlphaCorr=1.
Physical properties use standard values: water density 1000 kg/m3, kinematic viscosity 1e-6 m2/s; air density 1.225 kg/m3, kinematic viscosity 1.5e-5 m2/s.
Surface tension coefficient is set to 0.072 N/m with a contact angle of 90 degrees, or set to 0 if wall wetting effects are to be neglected; the dominant physics is gravity-driven sloshing at this scale.
The simulation is laminar (RAS off or laminar transport model) as the flow is not turbulent at this scale and Reynolds number.
All numerical values, boundary types, and solver parameters specified above are final and must not be altered.
